clinical_summary: EGFR blockade is combined with the oxaliplatin/fluorouracil/folinic-acid FOLFOX backbone to control selected metastatic colorectal cancer.
component_rationale: Cetuximab: Cetuximab attaches to EGFR on the outside of cells and blocks some growth messages. In this bowel-cancer plan, validated extended RAS testing helps identify whether treatment is suitable. Healthy skin also uses EGFR, so skin and nail effects need early care. Oxaliplatin: Oxaliplatin makes links within DNA. These interfere with copying and repair, which can stop a cancer cell dividing. Healthy tissues can also be affected. Folinic acid: Folinic acid helps fluorouracil remain bound to an enzyme needed to make DNA. In this regimen it increases fluorouracil activity and can also increase its unwanted effects. It is not a vitamin supplement to start yourself. Fluorouracil: Fluorouracil interferes with the production and use of DNA and RNA, the instructions cells need to grow. The infusion extends exposure over approximately two days.
schedule_context: Cetuximab on Day 1 and Day 8. FOLFOX4 starts on Day 1: oxaliplatin, folinic acid and fluorouracil bolus, followed by a 22-hour fluorouracil infusion. Day 2 includes folinic acid, another fluorouracil bolus and a second 22-hour infusion; finish around Day 3. Repeat every 14 days while beneficial and tolerable.
key_points: Cetuximab on Day 1 and Day 8. FOLFOX4 starts on Day 1: oxaliplatin, folinic acid and fluorouracil bolus, followed by a 22-hour fluorouracil infusion. Day 2 includes folinic acid, another fluorouracil bolus and a second 22-hour infusion; finish around Day 3. Repeat every 14 days while beneficial and tolerable.

important_cautions: Apply this exact regimen’s thresholds and exclusions; shared drugs do not imply shared blood-count, bilirubin or renal-dose rules.
DPD deficiency, severe early fluorouracil toxicity or cardiac symptoms require prompt specialist action.
Severe infusion reactions, significant skin toxicity, electrolyte loss, new pulmonary symptoms and corneal symptoms require assessment.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: Day 1 · chemotherapy and antibody: Moderate; Day 2 · FOLFOX4 fluorouracil/folinic acid: Low treatment-day risk; delayed Day 1 moderate-risk coverage still applies; Day 8 · weekly cetuximab only: Low
premedication_and_prophylaxis: Use the active-day support plan and current NCIS V8 guidance; reconcile all steroid, antiemetic and infusion-premedication orders.
Separate the Day 8 cetuximab-only plan from Day 1 chemotherapy support.
patient_education: Start the prescribed skin-care plan early, use moisturiser and sun protection, and report painful or infected skin or nails. Keep mineral blood-test appointments during treatment and for two months after cetuximab.
Follow your written rescue plan. Fever, blood, severe pain, reduced urine or inability to drink needs urgent advice.
Arrange Day 2 infusion renewal and final disconnection around Day 3. This is two separate 22-hour infusions; do not use a 46-hour pump timetable.

Avoid cold drinks and cold exposure as instructed after oxaliplatin; do not suck ice chips during fluorouracil in this regimen. Use prescribed anti-sickness medicines, pace activities and ask for nutritional, emotional or practical support.

Ask how and when the team will assess benefit, which blood tests continue during a pause, and what happens after the final dose. Mineral checks continue monthly for two months after the last antibody treatment.
Day 8 contains cetuximab only. Its premedicines and observation still matter, but the chemotherapy-day anti-sickness course is not automatically repeated.
special_support: Antiemetic classification refers to the active treatment day. Reconcile duplicate steroid entries before prescribing.
No automatic G-CSF schedule is added; use the patient’s neutropenia history, risk and consultant plan.
Cetuximab premedication and infusion observation remain necessary even on an antibody-only day.
Start local EGFR skin care; monitor magnesium, calcium and potassium before and periodically during therapy, then monthly for two months after the final dose.

Cold exposure can precipitate oxaliplatin neurotoxicity; do not recommend ice chips during fluorouracil in this combination. Review neuropathy every two cycles and sooner if symptoms interfere with function.
Confirm line care, pump contact details and disconnection arrangements; report chest pain, severe early fluorouracil toxicity or pump/line problems urgently.
FOLFOX4 Day 2 includes folinic acid and fluorouracil bolus followed by a second 22-hour infusion.
No repeat cetuximab or oxaliplatin is scheduled on Day 2.
NCIS multi-day guidance: cover the risk on each administered treatment day and delayed risk after treatment, using a reconciled prescription.
Cetuximab only: no irinotecan, oxaliplatin, fluorouracil or atropine is scheduled on Day 8.
Continue skin care, electrolyte monitoring, infusion precautions and the urgent contact plan.
Low-risk antibody-only antiemesis is distinct from Day 1 moderate-risk chemotherapy prophylaxis.

baseline: Confirm diagnosis, treatment line, goal, prior treatments, performance status, consent and all medicines.
Baseline FBC, renal and liver profile; assess infection, hydration, bowel symptoms and previous treatment toxicity.
Document validated extended RAS wild-type status for this colorectal pathway; do not infer it from unknown or KRAS exon 2-only testing.
Measure electrolytes including magnesium, calcium and potassium before treatment; correct abnormalities according to the prescription.
Ask specifically about prior antibody infusion reactions, red-meat allergy, tick bites and any known cetuximab IgE findings.
Document DPD assessment before the first fluorouracil dose unless already tested. Complete DPD deficiency excludes fluorouracil; partial deficiency needs a specialist dose plan.
ECG if cardiac function is compromised; no universal serial echo schedule is imposed. Confirm safe central access and pump training.
Record baseline peripheral neuropathy and functional impact.
before_each_cycle: Review symptoms, infection, hydration, bowel effects, medicines and previous-cycle toxicity; verify which components are actually being administered.
FBC, liver and renal profile before each cycle.
Repeat magnesium, calcium and potassium periodically during EGFR-antibody therapy and more frequently when abnormal; assess skin, nail, eye and pulmonary symptoms.
ongoing: Disease assessment and scan timing follow the supervising consultant’s treatment plan; do not hard-code a scan every fixed number of cycles.
There is no predetermined total course: review benefit, tolerability and patient priorities, and document continuation, pause, switch or stopping decisions.

NCCP post-treatment schedule: electrolytes, magnesium and calcium monthly for two months after the final antibody treatment. Panitumumab SmPC describes monitoring for up to eight weeks after completion; cetuximab SmPC specifies baseline and periodic monitoring during treatment.
Evaluate peripheral neuropathy every two cycles and review earlier if symptoms persist or impair function; cumulative toxicity may alter oxaliplatin independently of other components.
priority_toxicities: Rash, dry skin, cracks and sore nails
Infusion reaction; rare serious lung or skin effects
Persistent sensory neuropathy, sometimes lasting after treatment
Rare serious lung or blood complications
Severe early toxicity including DPD-related toxicity
urgent_review_signals: New breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse, severe diarrhoea or inability to drink require prompt assessment. Report eye pain, blurred vision, blistering or infected skin promptly. Call for line pain, swelling, leakage or unexpected pump progress.

longitudinal_schedule.note: The columns show order, not equal periods. There is no fixed number of cycles for these plans. Agree who books each check, when results are reviewed and whom to contact if a check is missed.

administration.cycle_and_sequence: Cetuximab on Day 1 and Day 8. FOLFOX4 starts on Day 1: oxaliplatin, folinic acid and fluorouracil bolus, followed by a 22-hour fluorouracil infusion. Day 2 includes folinic acid, another fluorouracil bolus and a second 22-hour infusion; finish around Day 3. Repeat every 14 days while beneficial and tolerable.
route_and_duration: The first weekly cetuximab infusion takes about two hours; later weekly infusions usually take about one hour. Oxaliplatin and folinic acid are usually infused over about two hours, before fluorouracil. Blood review, preparation, premedicines and observation add time; infusion time is not the total appointment length. Return on Day 2 for the second folinic-acid/fluorouracil part and renewal of the second 22-hour infusion. Final disconnection is planned around Day 3. This FOLFOX4 plan is not a single 46-hour infusion.
practical_workflow: Confirm the exact regimen, tests, medicines, emergency number and treatment goal. Discuss which central line is suitable and arrange pump training.

Return on Day 2 for the second folinic-acid/fluorouracil part and renewal of the second 22-hour infusion. Final disconnection is planned around Day 3. This FOLFOX4 plan is not a single 46-hour infusion.

Attend the separate Day 8 cetuximab-only visit. This is not another irinotecan or oxaliplatin day. Use the written symptom and support plan; do not wait for the next appointment if urgent symptoms appear.

Confirm the next visit after any delay or dose change. Treatment continues only while the oncology team judges benefit and tolerability acceptable. Follow-up mineral checks continue after the final EGFR-antibody dose where applicable.
observation_and_access: Resuscitation facilities and trained staff are required for infusions.
Allow for review, preparation and observation; quoted medicine infusion times are not total appointment times.

NCCP specifies observations before, during and after initial cetuximab infusions, with one-hour post-infusion observation after the first two doses; subsequent observation follows the regimen, reaction history and current product/local requirements.
First cetuximab infusion must respect the 5 mg/min maximum; subsequent maximum 10 mg/min. Do not promise a fixed two-hour visit for a large fortnightly dose.
Agree central access, ambulatory infusion arrangements and a documented pump problem/disconnection contact plan.
